chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The dowry (sadaq) of women during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was twelve waqiyah and a nash, its value in silver being five hundred dirhams.

key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: A silver coin, a unit of currency
key_terms.صَدَاقُ: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.نَشًّا: A smaller unit of weight/money, typically 1/3 of a waqiyah
key_terms.وَقِيَّةً: A unit of weight/money, typically 40 dirhams

ai.seo_question: What was the standard dowry amount during the time of the Prophet according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* establishes the baseline dowry (mahr) during the Prophet’s era as twelve waqiyah and a nash, equivalent to five hundred silver dirhams, reflecting the economic standards of early Medina. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration serves as a key reference for determining the 'mahr al-mithl' (standard dowry) when no specific amount is agreed upon, highlighting the tangible value placed on marital contracts in the Prophatic tradition.
